main_turf.bias_notes: Clockwise (right-handed). An exceptionally tight, circular track known as the 'Moonee Valley of the North' with one of the shortest home straights in Australia (only 143 metres). Because the home straight provides almost zero time to wind up, early speed ('E') and pocket pressers ('P') holding the fence command an overwhelming natural bias. Sweeping closers ('Swoopers') almost never make up ground on Good ground.
main_turf.post_bias: EXTREME INSIDE BARRIER BIAS: Inside barriers (stalls 1–4) are an immense advantage across all starts, especially the 800m, 1100m, and 1200m dashes. Outer draws (8+) face continuous ground loss around tight corners with no straightaway to recover.

handicapping_angles.the_extreme_speed_bias: Heavily upgrade pure front-runners ('E' types) and rail-skimming pressers with explosive 1st-call gate speed. Conversely, aggressively downgrade deep closers ('Swoopers'); if a horse is not in the first four rounding the turn, its winning chance is under 3%.
handicapping_angles.kilcoy_specialist_track_form: Because the geometry is so extreme, 'Horses for Courses' is a massive angle here. Upgrade horses with proven winning form specifically at Kilcoy, and apply caution to large-striding gallopers shipping in from wide tracks like Sunshine Coast or Eagle Farm.
handicapping_angles.se_qld_shipper_class_edge: Shippers from Toowoomba, Sunshine Coast, Gold Coast, and Ipswich midweeks step down into Kilcoy country benchmark ranks with a distinct class advantage (+3.0 pts).
handicapping_angles.the_kikuyu_cushion: The track is covered in dense Kikuyu grass cushion that holds together well during rain. Wet track ratings (Soft/Heavy) play slightly faster than standard dirt-based country tracks.
